findings.claim: Image caption: 'Image created with Google Gemini Pro'
findings.issue: Not a factual error — 'Gemini Pro' remains a current product tier (the current version is Gemini 3.1 Pro, released in preview Feb 19, 2026). The generic 'Gemini Pro' label is fine as a tool attribution and does not present a stale lineup as current. Flagged only for awareness.

findings.claim: Markdown formatting: 'a phenomenon called \*\*hallucination\*\*' and the caption's unclosed italic '*Image created with...'
findings.issue: Escaped asterisks (\*\*) will render as literal backslash-asterisks rather than bold, and the caption's leading '*' opens italics that are never closed. These are rendering/style issues, not factual findings, but they will visibly affect the published page.

newData.body:
A curated collection of the best places to learn more about AI, large language models, and the broader landscape. ### **Foundational Reading**

Attention Is All You Need — Original Transformer Paper

The 2017 Google research paper that introduced the Transformer architecture which underpins every modern LLM.

AcademicArchitecture

arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 ↗

The Illustrated Transformer — Jay Alammar

The clearest visual explanation of how transformers work. Essential reading for anyone wanting to understand the mechanics without heavy maths.

VisualBeginner-friendly

jalammar.github.io ↗

Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3 Paper)

OpenAI's landmark 2020 paper introducing GPT-3 and the concept of few-shot learning at scale.

AcademicOpenAI

arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165 ↗
### **Courses & Interactive Learning**

fast.ai — Practical Deep Learning for Coders

Free, hands-on course that takes you from basics to building real neural networks. No heavy maths prerequisites.

FreeCoursePractical

course.fast.ai ↗

Andrej Karpathy — Neural Networks: Zero to Hero

YouTube series by former Tesla and OpenAI researcher. Builds a neural network from scratch in Python. One of the best free resources available.

FreeYouTubeCoding

YouTube Playlist ↗

DeepLearning.AI Short Courses

Short courses on LLMs, prompt engineering, RAG, and agents, taught by Andrew Ng and leading practitioners. Many run about one to two hours and, as of 2026-07-21, are free to access during the DeepLearning.AI learning platform beta. Ideal for non-technical learners.

FreeCourseBeginner-friendly

deeplearning.ai/courses ↗
### **News & Commentary**

The Batch — DeepLearning.AI Newsletter

Weekly AI news and commentary for engineers, executives, and enthusiasts, with a personal letter from Andrew Ng in every issue. Clear, balanced, and accessible for non-technical readers.

NewsletterWeekly

deeplearning.ai/the-batch ↗

Import AI — Jack Clark

Detailed weekly newsletter from Jack Clark, co-founder and Head of Policy at Anthropic. Covers research, policy, and the strategic AI landscape. Read it on his own site, which is the canonical home for the archive.

NewsletterResearch

jack-clark.net ↗

Simon Willison's Blog

Practical, technically sharp commentary on LLM developments — how they actually work, what they are good at, and where they fail. Written by an independent researcher and open-source maintainer.

BlogTechnical

simonwillison.net ↗
### **Model Playgrounds**

Ollama — Run models locally

Download and run open-weight models on your own computer. Free, private, no API costs.

FreeLocalOpen source

ollama.com ↗

Hugging Face — Model Hub

The GitHub of AI models. Browse, download, and test thousands of open models. Essential reference for the open AI ecosystem.

FreeModelsCommunity

huggingface.co ↗
newData.title: Interesting Resources

findings.claim: OpenAI's GPT-5.5 is the current flagship
findings.issue: Stale flagship claim — the exact failure mode this pipeline must catch. GPT-5.5 has been superseded. OpenAI launched the GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, Luna) for general availability on July 9, 2026, with GPT-5.6 Sol as the new flagship (following a limited preview begun June 26, 2026). The card describes a superseded lineup as current and does not mention GPT-5.6 at all. The models list ('GPT-5.5 (Thinking / Pro) · GPT-5.5 Instant · GPT-5.4') is likewise out of date and should include the GPT-5.6 tier at the top.

findings.claim: GPT-5.5 Instant has been the default model across ChatGPT since May 5, 2026.
findings.issue: This is accurate and remains true even after GPT-5.6's launch — GPT-5.5 Instant remains the everyday default while GPT-5.6 Sol powers higher reasoning tiers on paid plans. No correction needed, but worth confirming the card retains this line when it is updated for GPT-5.6, since a naive update might wrongly replace the default.

findings.claim: o3 itself on a sunset path through August 2026
findings.issue: Consistent with sources: OpenAI's release notes state o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period. Consider stating the specific date (Aug 26, 2026) for precision, but not a blocking issue.

findings.claim: Anthropic's newest and most capable model, Fable 5, remains suspended for all users as of this writing under a US export-control directive.
findings.issue: This is stale and now false. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were suspended on June 12, 2026, but the US Commerce Department lifted the export controls on June 30, 2026, and Anthropic restored Fable 5 globally on July 1, 2026. As of today (2026-07-21), Fable 5 is available, not suspended. Presenting the suspension as the current state of the world is a blocking error.

findings.claim: ...remains suspended for all users as of this writing...
findings.issue: House-rule violation: a bare 'as of this writing' with no explicit date is a BLOCKING finding on its own. An explicit date is required for any 'as of' statement. (This compounds the factual error above.)

findings.claim: Claude Opus 4.8 offers the highest accessible capability for complex reasoning and writing tasks.
findings.issue: This presents a superseded position as current. Since Fable 5's restoration on July 1, 2026, Anthropic describes Claude Fable 5 (the generally available Mythos-class model) as its most capable widely released model, sitting above the Opus tier. Opus 4.8 is the top Opus-tier model but not the highest accessible capability overall. The card also omits Fable 5 from the lineup entirely while internally acknowledging it as 'newest and most capable,' which is contradictory.

findings.claim: Anthropic eliminated its long-context pricing surcharge in March 2026, so Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 4.6 now support a 1-million-token context window at flat per-token rates via the API.
findings.issue: The March 13, 2026 surcharge removal applied to Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6; Opus 4.8 did not exist until May 28, 2026. Opus 4.8 does support 1M-token context at flat rates today, so the end-state claim is correct, but attributing Opus 4.8's flat pricing to the March 2026 change is chronologically imprecise. Haiku 4.5 (mentioned in the lineup) has a 200K context window and was not part of this change.

findings.claim: Gemini 3.5 Flash ... measures as the fastest output speed of any major frontier model.
findings.issue: This superlative is false as of July 2026. Independent speed leaderboards (Artificial Analysis-based) show the diffusion model Mercury 2 by Inception as the output-speed leader at roughly 789 tokens/second, and among high-intelligence models GPT-5.4 leads at about 74 tok/s. Gemini 3.5 Flash does not appear as the top output-speed model in any current benchmark. Google positions 3.5 Flash as 'near-Pro intelligence at Flash-tier speed/cost,' not as the outright fastest model. Recommend removing the superlative or reframing it as 'optimised for high throughput.'

findings.claim: Gemini 3.1 Pro & Gemini 3.5 Flash (presented as the current lineup)
findings.issue: The lineup is accurate and current as of 2026-07-21: Gemini 3.5 Flash is GA (launched May 19, 2026) and is the model behind gemini-flash-latest; the Pro flagship is Gemini 3.1 Pro (gemini-3-pro-preview now redirects to 3.1 Pro). Worth flagging for monitoring only: Gemini 3.5 Pro was announced at I/O (May 19, 2026) and has repeatedly slipped (June, then July), so a new premium flagship may land imminently and supersede 3.1 Pro. No change needed now, but this card will go stale quickly if 3.5 Pro ships.

findings.claim: Gemini 3.1 Pro supports a 1-million-token context window.
findings.issue: Correct — 1M tokens is the reliably supported commercial window for the current Gemini family. Note that some third-party sources cite 'up to 2 million tokens' for parts of the Gemini lineup; the 1M figure the card uses is the safe, well-supported number, so this is informational only.

findings.claim: xAI's Grok 4.3 ... is the current flagship in the Grok family
findings.issue: Stale lineup presented as current — the exact failure mode this check targets. As of July 8, 2026, Grok 4.5 is xAI's current flagship. xAI's own docs say 'For everything else, including code, use Grok 4.5. It is the most intelligent and fastest model we've built,' and the API 'grok-latest'/quickstart examples default to grok-4.5. Grok 4.3 is now the cheaper long-context secondary tier, not the flagship. Today is 2026-07-21, so 4.5 has been out ~2 weeks.

findings.claim: models: 'Grok 4.3 · Grok 4.1 · Grok 4 Fast'
findings.issue: The current model list is wrong. The actual current lineup is Grok 4.5 (flagship), Grok 4.3 (lower-cost 1M-context tier), and Grok 4.1 Fast (budget/volume tier). 'Grok 4 Fast' was deprecated on 2026-05-15 and retires 2026-08-15, so it should not be presented as a current available model. Grok 4.5 is missing entirely.

findings.claim: Earlier variants — Grok 4 and Grok 4 Fast — remain available for lighter or faster use cases.
findings.issue: Grok 4 Fast is deprecated (2026-05-15) and retires 2026-08-15; per multiple sources the original Grok 4 was also retired/redirected to newer models in a May 2026 cleanup. Presenting these as currently available for everyday use is inaccurate. The genuinely current lighter/faster tier is Grok 4.1 Fast (2M context).

findings.claim: with a 1-million-token context window
findings.issue: This figure is correct for Grok 4.3, but if the card is corrected to describe the current flagship Grok 4.5, that model has a 500K-token context window, not 1M. Ensure the context-window figure is paired with the correct model.

findings.claim: released in 2026, is the current flagship
findings.issue: The card contains no explicit 'as of <date>' qualifier. Given how rapidly xAI's lineup changes (4.3 in April, 4.5 in July), the house rule favors an explicit dated 'as of' statement so freshness is auditable. Not blocking on its own, but worth adding when correcting the flagship.

findings.claim: Meta's Llama 4 family remains the most widely deployed open-weight AI ecosystem. / models: Llama 4 Maverick · Llama 4 Scout · Llama 3.3 70B
findings.issue: The card's headline framing presents Llama 4 as Meta's current frontier lineup, but as of April 8, 2026 Meta pivoted to the proprietary Muse Spark (built by Meta Superintelligence Labs) as its frontier effort and the engine behind Meta AI. The draft's own description does disclose this pivot, so the content is not stale — but the lead sentence and 'models' field understate the shift. Consider clarifying that Llama 4 is the current open-weight lineup while Muse Spark is now Meta's frontier model.

findings.claim: Meta's Llama 4 family remains the most widely deployed open-weight AI ecosystem.
findings.issue: This is a present-tense currency claim ('remains ... most widely deployed') with no date anchor. Not a blocking date-rule violation (no bare 'as of writing/today' phrase is used), but a superlative-plus-present-tense claim like this is hard to verify and would benefit from an explicit date or softening.

findings.claim: In April 2026, Meta Superintelligence Labs launched a new proprietary model, Muse Spark
findings.issue: Accurate but imprecise. The specific launch date was April 8, 2026. Also, developments have since advanced: Muse Spark 1.1 entered public preview around July 9, 2026 with a paid developer API — the draft's characterization of Muse Spark as newly launched and proprietary remains correct, but a more current card could note the 1.1 release.

findings.claim: Muse Spark is the current model from Meta Superintelligence Labs (models: 'Muse Spark').
findings.issue: Stale lineup presented as current. Meta released Muse Spark 1.1 on July 9, 2026 as its second MSL model and a significant upgrade over the original Muse Spark; it is now the model running in the Meta AI app and at meta.ai (in 'Thinking' mode). The card describes only the original Muse Spark in the present tense without mentioning 1.1, so it presents a superseded state of the world as current. Update to reflect that Muse Spark 1.1 is the current model as of July 2026.

findings.claim: API access is limited to a private preview for select developers.
findings.issue: No longer current. On July 9, 2026 Meta launched a PUBLIC preview of the new Meta Model API, where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1 (self-serve, US developers, at $1.25/M input and $4.25/M output tokens). 'Private preview for select developers' was accurate at the April launch but is stale as a present-tense claim.

findings.claim: "It is currently accessible through the Meta AI app and meta.ai website, with API access limited to a private preview..."
findings.issue: House-rule violation: a present-tense 'currently' claim about a fast-changing fact carries no explicit date. Per the required-date rule, an undated 'currently/as of' statement is blocking. Add an explicit 'as of <date>' anchor (and correct the underlying facts, which have changed since April).

findings.claim: $14.3 billion stake in Scale AI brought in Alexandr Wang as chief AI officer.
findings.issue: Accurate. The $14.3 billion figure for a 49% stake (valuing Scale at ~$29 billion) and Wang becoming Meta's first Chief AI Officer leading Meta Superintelligence Labs are both confirmed. No change needed; noted only for completeness.

findings.claim: Muse Spark launched April 8, 2026 as the first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs; weights are not open; Meta hopes to open-source future versions; it replaced Llama as the model powering Meta AI across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, meta.ai and smart glasses.
findings.issue: These historical/framing facts are all confirmed and correct. The problem is not their accuracy but that the surrounding present-tense framing omits the July 9, 2026 Muse Spark 1.1 update (see blocking findings).

findings.claim: matching OpenAI o1's reasoning benchmark performance at a fraction of the training cost of Western frontier labs
findings.issue: The 'benchmark parity with o1' claim is well supported. However, the specific 'fraction of the training cost' framing is the weakest part: the most widely verified cost comparison is inference/API cost (~30x cheaper per Epoch AI), while DeepSeek's reported training cost was itself publicly disputed at the time of the R1 release, with analysts noting it may have been underreported. The claim is historically defensible but would be more accurate as 'inference/API cost' or with a caveat. Not embarrassing to the site, hence a note rather than blocking.

findings.claim: DeepSeek V4 Pro is the current flagship ... Both are available as open weights and via the DeepSeek API.
findings.issue: Accurate as of the check date, but the shipped V4 Pro/Flash are officially 'preview' releases (launched April 24, 2026). A general-availability (GA) V4 release with revised pricing was rumored/imminent around mid-July 2026. Consider adding an explicit dated qualifier (e.g. 'as of July 2026, the V4 preview...') so the card doesn't silently go stale when GA lands. Note only — the lineup named is genuinely the current one.

findings.claim: Alibaba's Qwen3.6 family [presented as the current model lineup: Qwen3.6-Max-Preview, Qwen3.6-Plus, Qwen3.6-27B]
findings.issue: The Qwen3.6 family is no longer current; it is two generations behind. Alibaba released Qwen3.7 (Max and Plus variants) in May/June 2026, and previewed the flagship Qwen3.8-Max-Preview (a claimed 2.4-trillion-parameter model) on July 19, 2026. Presenting Qwen3.6 as the current lineup is exactly the stale-lineup failure mode. The card should feature Qwen3.8-Max-Preview / Qwen3.7 as current, or explicitly frame the 3.6 family as historical/the current open-weight line.

findings.claim: All are available as open weights
findings.issue: False for two of the three named models. Qwen3.6-Max-Preview is proprietary/API-only with no published weights, and Qwen3.6-Plus is a proprietary API model (not Apache 2.0, requires an Alibaba Cloud account). Only Qwen3.6-27B is genuinely open-weight (Apache 2.0, released April 22, 2026). The claim also contradicts the card's own earlier description of Max-Preview and Plus as 'cloud-served' options.

findings.claim: Qwen3.6-27B ... as a dense, self-hostable model aimed at coding and agentic tasks
findings.issue: This specific claim is accurate: Qwen3.6-27B is a dense, Apache 2.0, self-hostable model built for agentic coding. No correction needed, but it is the only one of the three named models that matches the 'open weights' description.

findings.claim: Qwen's open-weight ecosystem has become one of the most actively used on Hugging Face, alongside DeepSeek and Llama.
findings.issue: Well-supported and reasonable (200,000+ Qwen model variations on Hugging Face). Not a problem.

findings.claim: Kimi K2.6 ... the general-purpose K2.6 flagship (presented as the current flagship, with the model lineup listed as K2.6 / K2.7 Code / K2.5)
findings.issue: Stale flagship presented as current. Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 16, 2026 (five days before today's date of 2026-07-21), and K3 — a ~2.8T-parameter MoE with a 1M-token context window — is now the flagship and the explicit successor to the entire K2 family (K2, K2.5, K2.6, K2.7 Code). The draft describes a superseded lineup as the current state of the world, which is exactly the failure mode being guarded against. The card should present K3 as the current flagship, or reframe the K2.x models as historical/prior releases.

findings.claim: Kimi K2.6, released April 2026 ... Kimi K2.7 Code, released June 2026
findings.issue: The individual dates check out (K2.6 released April 20, 2026; K2.7 Code released June 12, 2026), but calling K2.6 the 'general-purpose flagship' while K2.7 Code (a higher version number) already exists is confusing without noting that K2.7 Code is a coding-specialized fork of K2.6, not a general-purpose successor. Sources confirm Moonshot positions K2.7 Code as a complement to K2.6, not a replacement — the draft's framing is roughly right on this point but would be clearer stated explicitly. Moot in any case once K3 is acknowledged as flagship.

findings.claim: open-sourced under a modified MIT license ... available ... self-hosted using Hugging Face weights
findings.issue: Accurate for the K2 family (K2.6 and K2.7 Code are on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license). No correction needed; noted only for completeness. Note that K3's open weights were dated for release by July 27, 2026, so if K3 is added, its weight-availability status should be stated with that caveat.

findings.claim: now the default in Mistral's own Vibe and Le Chat tools
findings.issue: Medium 3.5 is indeed the default model in Vibe/Le Chat, but as of May 28, 2026 Mistral rebranded Le Chat as 'Vibe' (Le Chat became Vibe Work/Chat mode). Presenting 'Vibe and Le Chat' as two separate current products is slightly stale; they are now one product (Vibe), with Le Chat's chat experience surviving as a mode. Not factually wrong enough to embarrass the site, but consider updating to reflect the merged branding.

findings.claim: Mistral Medium 3.5 is the newest
findings.issue: Among the three models in this card's lineup, Medium 3.5 (released ~April 28-30, 2026) is the most recent. However, Mistral has shipped later models not in this card (e.g., a 'Leanstral 1.5' dated 2026-07-02 appears in sources). The phrasing 'the newest' is scoped to this lineup and reads fine, but strictly it is not Mistral's newest overall release as of 2026-07-21.

findings.claim: Mistral Medium 3.5 ... released as open weights
findings.issue: Accurate that it is open weights, but for precision note the specific license is a 'Modified MIT License' (not Apache 2.0, which applies to Large 3 and Small 4). The draft does not misstate this, but the distinction is worth flagging since the two sibling models in the same card are Apache 2.0.

spotAuditFindings.issue: GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) reached general availability on July 9, 2026 across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, becoming OpenAI's flagship family; the tracker still lists only 'GPT-5.5 (Thinking / Pro)'. This is the biggest launch of the month and its absence would look like an oversight.
Grok 4.5 launched publicly July 8, 2026 (Cursor-trained coding model, ~$2/$6 per 1M tokens); the tracker still lists 'Grok 4.3'.

Claude Sonnet 5 launched June 30, 2026 (1M-token context, now the claude.ai default at intro pricing of $2/$10, rising to $3/$15 after Aug 31, 2026); the tracker still lists 'Claude Sonnet 4.6'. Note the upcoming Aug 31 price change is itself time-sensitive.

Kimi K3 (Moonshot, ~2.8T params) was announced July 16, 2026 and reportedly edges past Claude Opus 4.8 on independent rankings, with open weights due July 27, 2026; the tracker still lists 'Kimi K2.6'. Emerging item worth reflecting given the imminent weight release.
